races.name: Get Best Odds With Oddschecker Maiden Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Brosna Town
runners_data.note: Holds a place in Good-ground form and has some experience over similar trips, but is a genuine hold-up horse whose natural style is held up at the rear — in a field already crowded with closers it will likely find itself without cover and without the late pace to bring opponents back; 5yo with 3lb claim in the saddle for a trainer cold over 14 days.

runners_data.name: Credit Union
runners_data.note: Trainer Jessica Bedi is 0/3 over the past fortnight and this horse has finished outside the places in all three hurdle starts to date, including a pair of 10th-place finishes on Good; naturally races from the rear but the hold-up ranks are congested, so it may travel in a more forward position than suits — a fader who hasn't shown enough yet.

runners_data.name: Eagle One
runners_data.note: An 8yo returning after 200 days off with a sparse hurdles profile, though placed form over fences on Soft and Standard; the good ground here is fine on history but the layoff is significant, and as a natural hold-up type it faces the same positioning squeeze as several others in this field.

runners_data.name: Ifyouhaveaplan
runners_data.note: Holds a genuine prominent racing style which suits this pace scenario well — sat behind Way Maker and can travel without racing keenly; two runs on Good this season, both below-par finishes, but the style fit is correct and Louise Allan's yard has a horse in the right slot for how the race will flow.

runners_data.name: Jentobello
runners_data.note: Excellent place record in similar going — 2 wins and 5 places from 6 runs on Good, including wins over 16f and placed efforts over 20f — and a genuine prominent style that slots neatly behind a sole front-runner; trainer Iain Jardine is 6/35 over 14 days, suggesting some recent form, and the 298-day absence is the key query, but the profile fits this shape very well.

runners_data.name: Just Keeps Rolling
runners_data.note: Wears a hood (hg:p) and has pulled up on multiple recent starts — form string shows P-P-P in recent hurdles — and 105 days off doesn't inspire confidence; as a hold-up type it faces the same positional congestion as several others and has given no reason to think it can make use of whatever position it finds.

runners_data.name: Way Maker
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner and likely to dictate a comfortable, unhurried gallop from the front; OR 105 is the lowest in the field but the pace control is the asset here — has shown placed form over this sort of trip and trip distance on Good, and James Bowen knows how to exploit a lead for the Bowen yard; wears a hood (hg:p) and has run 41 days ago.

runners_data.name: Arcimboldo
runners_data.note: A 4yo returning just 15 days after a pull-up (P) on debut, trained by Mike Sowersby who is 0/2 in the 14-day window; the horse's natural style is hold-up but with so many closers, it will be squeezed into an unnatural midfield berth and has yet to complete a hurdle race — the short turnaround adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Centurion's Sister
runners_data.note: Consistent placer — 0 wins but 5 places from 10 runs on Good, including three 2nds — and a natural prominent style that puts her in exactly the right position for this pace structure behind Way Maker; Danny McMenamin is an accomplished northern jockey and she has dropped to OR 98, which gives her a weight advantage; the lack of a win is the nagging concern.

runners_data.name: Park Hall
runners_data.note: Two runs in, two places, one win — very lightly raced but the best recent form figures in the field and Harry Skelton aboard for the powerful Dan Skelton yard; races with a hood (hg:h) and is a genuine hold-up type, so relies on the pace being strong enough to bring rivals back — on a steady gallop set by Way Maker alone that is the risk, even if the class is there.

races.paceDynamic: Way Maker is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no meaningful challengers for the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 2m4½f trip on Good ground at Market Rasen. The pace is unlikely to be particularly fierce, meaning the race will be run to suit horses who can travel comfortably within striking range and pick up off a steady tempo rather than those needing a truly searching test to bring rivals back to them. Jentobello, Centurion's Sister, and Ifyouhaveaplan are the genuine prominent types who should sit close behind Way Maker and be best positioned to take advantage of the manageable fractions. The field does contain more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Park Hall, Eagle One, Credit Union, Arcimboldo, and Brosna Town are all natural hold-up horses, and with so many in the same role, several will be forced into a more prominent position than they prefer or will need to find more ground late than the pace is likely to create; those sitting closest to the pace — Jentobello and Centurion's Sister — are the style profiles this race shape favours most clearly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Way Maker Leads, Closers Chase
scenarios.trigger: If Way Maker sets a steady, uncontested gallop and the race develops into a test of jumping and staying power from three out.
scenarios.body: Way Maker controls fractions, the field strings out into their natural order, and the prominent holders — Jentobello and Centurion's Sister — travel into contention without burning energy early; horses further back face too much ground to make up off a moderate pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens earlier than expected and the race becomes a genuine stamina test, exposing hold-up horses who cannot close.
scenarios.body: Jentobello or Ifyouhaveaplan sit close to the pace and kick on from two out, with the steady tempo having preserved enough energy to sustain their run; horses redistributed from the rear lack the finishing kick to bridge the gap.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Park Hall Powers Late
scenarios.trigger: If Park Hall is produced with a well-timed late challenge and the pace is strong enough to set up a closer.
scenarios.body: Park Hall has smart form on Good ground and a professional yard behind it with Harry Skelton aboard, giving it the class to run down a weakening leader if the fractions suit a finisher; this scenario requires the pace to be stronger than Way Maker alone is likely to generate, making it dependent on a racing scenario that is less probable.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Melee Disrupts Order
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Credit Union, Arcimboldo, Brosna Town — cause interference or overcrowding in the pack, scrambling the race shape.
scenarios.body: With multiple natural hold-up types forced into unfamiliar midfield positions, traffic issues or jumping mistakes in the pack could compromise several fancied runners and hand the advantage to whoever has cleanest passage; this is the least reliable scenario because it depends on horses racing out of role and a degree of chance.

watchPoints.text: Way Maker sets the early pace unopposed — if James Bowen gets a soft lead and dictates fractions, the race advantage belongs entirely to prominent types like Jentobello and Centurion's Sister from the moment the tape rises.

Park Hall is the class danger from off the pace, but Harry Skelton will need Way Maker to quicken the tempo in the back straight to create the gaps a hold-up horse needs — watch whether the pace is genuinely strong enough to bring Park Hall into it from three out.
Arcimboldo runs just 15 days after pulling up on debut — watch early to see if the horse settles and jumps cleanly, as another jumping error could bring others down in the field.

With Credit Union, Brosna Town, Arcimboldo, Eagle One, Park Hall, and Just Keeps Rolling all natural hold-up types, the midfield and rear will be densely packed — watch for traffic issues and checked runs between the final bend and the last hurdle.

Jentobello returns after 298 days off — watch how sharply it moves to post and how its jumping holds up in the early stages, as a long absence for a prominent racer in a field with a sole front-runner means it must jump well from the start to hold its position.

races.name: Bet Smarter With Oddschecker+ Novices' Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Eternal Angel
runners_data.note: Six-year-old mare with two wins at 16f on good ground for Tom Lacey, races in headgear (hg:h) and has strong similar-going form (8 from 11); Jonathan Burke pairs up here and she maps as a natural leader who will press Loriko hard from the off, though her last run was a distant fifth at 22f suggesting that trip was too far and coming back to 2m½f plays to her strengths.

runners_data.name: Loriko
runners_data.note: Dan and Harry Skelton combination is the key angle — this five-year-old tops the OR ratings at 125 and has won twice and placed seven times on similar ground, giving him the strongest profile in the race; his natural front-running style suits dictating here and Skelton's course management should allow him to manage the pace duel with Eternal Angel without burning himself out.

runners_data.name: Destination Unkown
runners_data.note: Michael Chapman's lightly-framed hold-up horse carries a very low OR of 58 and a consistent record of fading in the final stages — his recent form string of PP-7 reflects that tendency; James Best will ride him from behind but the probability of closing on two class front-runners on good ground is slim, and stamina concerns over 2m½f compound the difficulty.

runners_data.name: Mayo
runners_data.note: Mickey Bowen's son, ridden by James Bowen, has a hold-up profile but has not won in four attempts on good ground (0W1P); the 70-day absence is the most significant flag here and while three of his four runs have been at 16f on good, he needs the front two to empty themselves before he can get competitive, which is an uncertain dependency in this small field.

races.paceDynamic: Loriko and Eternal Angel are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this 2m½f trip at Market Rasen on good ground, creating a genuine, sustained gallop rather than a dawdle. Harry Skelton on Loriko (OR 125, the class-highest in the field) and Jonathan Burke on Eternal Angel (OR 120, two wins at 16f on good) will push each other along, meaning neither is likely to steal an uncontested rhythm — the pace will be honest and consistent throughout. Mayo and Destination Unknown are both held-up types sitting a distance behind, but with OR ratings of 58 and 120 respectively they represent very different threats from off the pace. This contested front-running shape favours whichever of the two leaders travels better into the back straight and can assert jumping fluency — prominent and lead profiles are most favoured here, while the hold-up horses face a stern task if the leaders control tempo without overdoing it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leaders Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Loriko and Eternal Angel share the front and the pace remains honest but controlled, setting up a two-horse duel from three out.
scenarios.body: The superior OR and Skelton's tactical nous give Loriko the edge to lead into the straight and use jumping ability to grind Eternal Angel down; Eternal Angel's two wins at 16f on good show she stays and jumps well enough to match strides to the last. Both leaders benefit as the hold-up horses simply can't close the gap on a good-ground, honest gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Breaks Clear Early
scenarios.trigger: If Loriko dominates from the front and Eternal Angel cracks under pressure, allowing Skelton to dictate a solo leader's pace.
scenarios.body: Loriko, with a higher OR and strong recent good-ground form (2W7P sim-going), settles into a rhythm that saps the others on the run to the final two hurdles and kicks clear; with only three rivals and no genuine chaser in behind, a clear lead by the home turn becomes very hard to peg back. This scenario rewards the class front-runner who can convert a contested early lead into a controlled solo break.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the front two burn each other out over-jumping or setting a frantic pace, leaving Mayo to produce a well-timed late run.
scenarios.body: Mayo has placed at 16f on good ground twice in four runs and James Bowen knows the horse well, though 70 days off is a concern; if the leaders crack badly in the final quarter-mile, Mayo's hold-up style finally gives him a target to run at. This scenario is possible but depends on front-runners genuinely over-cooking it, which is less likely with only four runners and experienced handlers controlling the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Flat Finish
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or fatigue disrupt the leaders in the closing stages, creating a messy, slowly-run finale.
scenarios.body: A hurdling mistake from either leader in the final two flights could level the playing field and let Mayo or even Destination Unknown stay in contention longer than expected; however Destination Unknown's consistent record of fading in finishes and a very low OR of 58 make this an unlikely winning path for the hold-up pair. This is the least probable shape and essentially requires multiple things to go wrong for the two class front-runners simultaneously.

watchPoints.text: Watch Loriko's jumping at the early flights — if Harry Skelton meets a hurdle wrong under pressure from Eternal Angel, it could fracture the duel and hand initiative to the field.

Monitor whether Eternal Angel tries to go with Loriko stride for stride from the outset; if she over-commits chasing the higher-rated rival, she may weaken into the straight and hand a clear run to Mayo.

Mayo's 70-day absence is the main fitness flag in the race — watch his movement in the paddock and whether James Bowen gives him an easy introduction or asks him to close early, which would suggest confidence in his fitness.

Destination Unknown's history of fading in finishes means his race will likely be run by three out — track whether he is still on the bridle approaching the second-last, as that would be an unusually strong sign for this horse.

With only four runners on good ground at Market Rasen, the gallop is unlikely to be truly suicidal — watch the early pace to see if either leader deliberately backs off to try and produce a sprint finish, which would reset the shape toward Scenario C.

races.name: Download The Oddschecker App Handicap Steeple Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: My Friend Sean
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer for Tom Lacey and Jonathan Burke who has a solid record on Good ground (9 runs, 3 wins, 5 places similar going), returning after a straightforward 31-day break; the tongue strap is noted and his two recent placed efforts at 2m4f and 2m4½f suggest the step back in trip to 2m1f is a live question, but his proximity racing style suits the anticipated pace shape.

runners_data.name: Belle Le Grand
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton and Dan Skelton combine with a mare who landed a recent win at 17f on Good ground and has been placed on this surface consistently; a genuine hold-up operator who will need the pace to be truly honest to get competitive, and with the rear end already congested, finding a clear run late is her primary tactical concern.

runners_data.name: Dog Fox
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor partners a 6-year-old with an impressive 13-from-15 record on Good ground who races prominently; the recent form includes a pulled-up run (P) and a void result (V) that need context but the going profile is hard to ignore, and Oliver Greenall & Josh Guerriero have him primed after a 22-day turnaround with 0/2 T14 suggesting no dramatic stable form concern.

runners_data.name: Ghasham
runners_data.note: Sam England's 7-year-old has been in consistent form — 1st, 2nd, 2nd in recent starts — and races from a hold-up position with genuine late pace; the trainer sends out 1 winner from 8 in the past 14 days which is modest, but the horse's own form on Good ground (7 runs, 1 win, 4 places) makes him the most credible back-marker if things develop cleanly ahead of him.

runners_data.name: Gower Prince
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Richie McLernon and the O'Neill yard, returning after an unusually long 101-day break which is the biggest flag against him; two recent runner-up efforts at Nottingham and elsewhere on Good ground show he belongs at this level, but his jumping record under pressure (headgear: hood) and fresh status need monitoring early over the fences.

runners_data.name: Clean Getaway
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's 9-year-old is a natural hold-up horse who has been pushed into a midfield map position because the rear is over-subscribed in this field; his Good-ground record is outstanding (14 from 15 similar runs) and he has won at this course, but the compromised starting position may prevent him from racing in his preferred patient manner, tempering his chance in a shape that requires a true late run.

runners_data.name: Miss Denver
runners_data.note: Sam Twiston-Davies takes the ride on this consistent mare who has been placed in all five recent starts without winning — a pattern worth noting — and whose natural instinct is to race from the rear; the race shape here pushes her to midfield rather than her preferred position, which means she is unlikely to have the late, fresh energy that a true hold-up run would generate, making her five-run no-win streak a concern.

runners_data.name: Genbu
runners_data.note: The youngest horse in the field at 4 years old, trained by Sarah-Jayne Davies and ridden by Charlie Price, Genbu is a confirmed front-runner whose form string (313354) shows activity and consistency rather than dominance; his jumping accuracy over fences at pace is the key watch point given his age and the fact that he will be asked to lead a handicap chase against more experienced rivals from the flag.

races.paceDynamic: Gower Prince and Genbu are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this 2m1f trip on good ground at Market Rasen, creating a genuinely contested gallop rather than a tactical crawl. That honest, pressured pace across the fences is likely to stretch the field and put a premium on jumping fluency and jumping stamina rather than a finishing kick. The field carries more pace than the map can absorb — Clean Getaway and Miss Denver are genuine hold-up types who have been redistributed to midfield positions because the rear is overcrowded in this shape, meaning their true running style may be compromised and their chance should be discounted in scenarios that depend on them closing from far back. This race shape — a contested lead with a genuine gallop — favours prominent-to-midfield horses with clean jumping records who can travel in the slipstream of the front two and pounce when the pace-setters tire, making My Friend Sean and Dog Fox the profile beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Gower Prince and Genbu force a genuine gallop and begin to tire from two out, allowing a prominent tracker to capitalise.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners set an honest pace that stretches the field jumping the railway fences, leaving them vulnerable late as a prominent racer travels smoothly behind and picks them off. My Friend Sean's consistent proximity and Dog Fox's strong Good-ground profile from a prominent pitch suit this shape perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Gower Prince or Genbu dictates a measured enough gallop to conserve energy and jumps their way clear in the straight.
scenarios.body: One of the two front-runners controls the fractions sufficiently to still be travelling when rivals crack, converting early position into a winning one. Gower Prince's two recent runner-up efforts on Good ground show the ability, while Genbu's consistent form string includes wins and multiple places over this trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly fierce and the front half of the field burns out, allowing a back-marker to pick through late.
scenarios.body: A burning pace from two front-runners could theoretically set things up for a late closer, but with Clean Getaway and Miss Denver not racing from their natural hold-up position, this scenario is weakened — they are redistributed types unlikely to fully execute a genuine late run. Ghasham has the most credible hold-up credentials and the form to benefit if he finds daylight, though his route to the front would need to be clear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Chaos, Errors Decide
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or fallers disrupt the front two and reduce the race to a test of survivorship through the final fences.
scenarios.body: With a young, lightly-experienced Genbu (age 4) up front and multiple runners carrying headgear, a mishap at a key fence could dramatically reshuffle the order. Dog Fox's 13-from-15 Good-ground hit rate and Belle Le Grand's recent win suggest they could pick through a scrambled field, though this is the least predictable outcome.

watchPoints.text: Gower Prince's 101-day absence is the single biggest flag in the race — monitor him in the paddock and at the first fence, as a rusty jumper up front could cause interference for the entire field.

Genbu's youth (4 years old) leading in a handicap chase on Good ground creates a jumping-accuracy risk; if he makes a significant error at an early fence, the entire front-running scenario collapses and the race is thrown open.

Clean Getaway and Miss Denver are genuine hold-up types racing out of their natural position — if neither can slot into the rear as intended, watch for crowding and interference in the midfield group between the railway fences.
Belle Le Grand needs a truly honest gallop to get competitive from her hold-up pitch; if Gower Prince and Genbu ease the pace at any stage, her chance evaporates before the straight.

Dog Fox's two question-mark results (V for void, P for pulled-up) in recent form need checking for context — if those runs have a benign explanation (jockey error, interference), his 13-from-15 Good-ground record becomes significantly more compelling than the raw form string suggests.

races.name: Oddschecker Free Bets Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Ernest Gray
runners_data.note: Solid prominent racer for Alan King, two wins from seven runs on Good ground and a recent second at this trip; Jonathan Burke takes over here and the horse has been consistent at 2m3-4f, though his OR of 121 means he carries top weight and his recent form includes a couple of disappointing runs that need explaining.

runners_data.name: Ballintubber Boy
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for the Twiston-Davies yard, outstanding record on Good going (13/15 placed or better) and visors fitted; uncontested lead over 2m7f plays entirely to his strengths, though he hasn't won from his last six starts and the question is whether he can convert his tactical advantage.

runners_data.name: Kiwi de Cotte
runners_data.note: Won last time out at 2m3f on Good for Dan and Harry Skelton, a combination who excel at placing horses; prominent style suits this shape perfectly and a 6-year-old still open to improvement, though he has pulled up twice in his form string which adds an element of risk.

runners_data.name: Belvedere Blast
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse for trainer Adrian Keatley, whose 14-day stats of 2/8 show some activity; Oakley Brown takes the 5lb claim which partially offsets the weight, but three consecutive placings at 2m4f on Good suggest he stays well — he needs things to go wrong for the front rank to make his challenge count.

runners_data.name: Lowlands
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type suited to the deepest rear position, with a win over 2m on Good for Nicky Richards and consistent placing record at staying trips; Danny McMenamin rides and the horse has placed four times from five on Good or Soft, making him the most credible closer in the field if the pace genuinely tests the leaders late.

runners_data.name: Parikarma
runners_data.note: Consistent placer at 2m2-4f on Good for Samuel Drinkwater, and Miss Imogen Mathias takes the 7lb claim — but this horse's natural running style sits at the rear, and the congested hold-up group means it is likely to race further forward than ideal, tempering the chance despite reasonable recent form figures of 3272.

races.paceDynamic: Ballintubber Boy is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of six over 2m7f on Good ground at Market Rasen, and with no rival willing or able to challenge for the lead, he is set to dictate an uncontested, measured gallop from the outset. Ernest Gray and Kiwi de Cotte will press forward into prominent positions just behind, forming a small chasing group, while Belvedere Blast, Lowlands, and Parikarma are nominally the hold-up brigade — though Parikarma's redistribution to midfield reflects that the genuine rear-rank slots are contested. With Ballintubber Boy able to control tempo and conserve energy over this stamina-testing trip, this race shape strongly favours the front-running and prominent profiles — those travelling close to the pace throughout will be best placed to strike from the final flight, leaving hold-up horses with a difficult task if the pace is never truly end-to-end searching. The field contains more hold-up horses than can all settle comfortably at the rear, and Lowlands and Belvedere Blast are most likely to actually secure the deepest positions, with Parikarma forced further forward than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ballintubber Boy Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Ballintubber Boy leads uncontested and sets a steady-to-fair pace, controlling the race from flag to finish.
scenarios.body: Ballintubber Boy exploits his front-running role perfectly over this stamina trip, rationing his effort before quickening from the last, while Ernest Gray and Kiwi de Cotte race prominently and are ideally positioned to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If Ernest Gray or Kiwi de Cotte track Ballintubber Boy closely and outstay him from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Ernest Gray, proven over this sort of trip on good ground with a win at 2m3f, or Kiwi de Cotte, unbeaten last time and in the care of Harry Skelton, uses their prominent position to collar the leader approaching the last.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finisher Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely searching and the front rank tie each other up, allowing Lowlands or Belvedere Blast to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: Lowlands, progressive over staying trips and with a recent win over 2m on good ground, would benefit most from a stamina test that exposes rivals who have gone too hard; Belvedere Blast placed at this trip recently but needs everything to fall right from his rear position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Parikarma Outrun Role
scenarios.trigger: If Parikarma, forced forward from its natural hold-up position, manages to find an unexpectedly comfortable racing pitch and sustains a challenge.
scenarios.body: Racing out of role with a style-fit discount and the amateur rider conceding further weight, this shape requires significant misjudgement from the field rather than genuine Parikarma superiority; the low OR of 97 makes the task steep against more fancied rivals.

watchPoints.text: Ballintubber Boy wears a visor — watch whether Sam Twiston-Davies uses the headgear to switch him on early; if he bucks or dwells at the start, his entire tactical advantage evaporates and the race shape changes fundamentally.

Kiwi de Cotte has two pull-ups in recent form (the P entries) — watch his jumping in the early stages, as any hesitancy could see Harry Skelton forced to push him along sooner than ideal, compromising his stamina reserves over 2m7f.

Lowlands must secure a genuine hold-up position to deliver his challenge — watch at the start and first two flights to see whether Danny McMenamin can get him settled well off the pace; if he is forced to race closer than ideal, his late-run profile is undermined.

Ernest Gray has had 39 days off since his last run — watch his initial jumping and early keenness under Jonathan Burke, as horses returning after a month-plus break can be exuberant early in handicap hurdles, which could compromise his prominent position if he runs too freely.

With only 6 runners over 2m7f on Good ground, the field is likely to string out quickly — watch for any horse that loses its position at the fourth or fifth hurdle, as making up ground over this trip at Market Rasen is notoriously difficult with a compliant leader setting the terms.

races.name: Oddschecker+ Subscription Service Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: The Clonmel Kid
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with a win from 8 runs on similar good going and last-time-out form that includes a course win over 20f; Philip Kirby's yard is cold (0/16 in 14 days) but the horse's profile suits a searching gallop over this trip, and blinkers (hg:p) suggest it needs to be switched on.|

runners_data.name: A Dublin Job
runners_data.note: Front-runner confirmed, partnered by 7lb claimer Johnstone-Baker which is a notable rider switch for this veteran; the horse has 3 wins from 15 starts on similar going but its recent form (P-6556) is uninspiring, and the weight of 165lbs may blunt its ability to dominate once pressed by La Quarite.|

runners_data.name: Ribeye
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old hold-up type whose best ground form shows some ability but whose recent record features two pull-ups (P) and a series of moderate finishes; Danny McMenamin takes the ride, but the age and jumping reliability over 2m5½f are real concerns.|

runners_data.name: Huckleberry Sting
runners_data.note: Sharp recent form (1-2312) and two wins from 11 starts on good ground make this the most credentialed hold-up horse in the field on ability — but the crowded rear-of-field picture means it is unlikely to find its natural berth, and its chance must be tempered accordingly.|

runners_data.name: La Quarite
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning from 340 days off, which is a significant fitness query even for Mickey Bowen's yard (0/2 in 14 days); best form is on good going with a win at 21f, and if fit enough James Bowen gives confidence, but the layoff is the dominant risk in assessing whether it can press from the front for 2m5½f.|

runners_data.name: Huit Reflets
runners_data.note: The sole genuine prominent-style runner sitting behind the two front-runners; Mark Walford's yard is in modest form (1/9 in 14 days) but this 9-year-old has placed twice at 20f on good and soft going, and Jamie Hamilton's booking is positive — tactically it is the best-placed of the non-leaders.|

runners_data.name: Uncle Al
runners_data.note: Won over 24f on good ground last time out (OR=83) and has placed form on similar surfaces, but pulled up twice in recent starts and the redistribution away from the rear is a genuine concern; Conor O'Farrell partners and the headgear (hg:p) suggests connections want it more engaged, though it remains a horse whose best chance comes when it can be produced late.|

runners_data.name: Fast Deal
runners_data.note: Bottom weight on OR=64 with a form string of FP-866 and no wins or places on good ground across the last five runs; James Best takes the ride but this is the weakest profile in the field on ratings, recent form and going record, and it too is a natural hold-up horse unable to find that position naturally in this shape.|

races.paceDynamic: A Dublin Job and La Quarite are the two confirmed front-runners in this field, and with both likely to press forward from the off, this race will be run at an honest, sustained gallop over 2m5½f on good ground at Market Rasen. A Dublin Job, ridden by the 7lb claimer Cameron Johnstone-Baker, may find La Quarite's presence under James Bowen forces both into a genuine duel across the first circuit, burning through energy at a rate that sets up the race for those able to track the pace comfortably or wait off it. The sustained gallop on a fair surface over this trip is a shape that classically suits a horse capable of travelling prominently or close enough to pounce without having to produce a sustained rally from far back. Huit Reflets, the only genuine prominent type behind the two leaders, is therefore well-placed tactically; note that Huckleberry Sting, Uncle Al, and Fast Deal are natural hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map because the rear of the field is already congested with their profile — all three are unlikely to secure a truly prominent pitch, meaning the tactical edge belongs to horses with the engine to travel in the first half of the race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace Grinds On
scenarios.trigger: If A Dublin Job and La Quarite fight out a genuine duel from the front and the honest gallop is sustained throughout.
scenarios.body: The two leaders press each other from flag to finish, emptying out the race for horses with stamina and the ability to close over the final two fences; the long trip on good ground rewards horses who have been racing within themselves behind the pace. Huit Reflets, travelling prominently throughout, and The Clonmel Kid, coming from off the pace with a hold-up style at a distance that suits, are the profiles that benefit most.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Dictates Solo
scenarios.trigger: If La Quarite (or A Dublin Job) establishes a clear lead early and the other fails to press, leaving a single front-runner to control tempo.
scenarios.body: With one horse controlling the fractions unchallenged, the pace becomes measured rather than brutal, allowing the leader to travel within itself and potentially kick clear at the last fence; La Quarite, returning from 340 days off but with strong course-type form on good ground, is the more interesting profile here if fit enough to handle the layoff. A Dublin Job's veteran consistency over course and distance distances makes it the alternative beneficiary if it is the one that gets clear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners tie each other up completely and the pace is truly searching, setting up a strong late rally from the rear.
scenarios.body: Huckleberry Sting and Uncle Al, both genuine hold-up horses in this field who are mapped to midfield due to redistribution, would need to find more space than this race shape naturally affords them — making this scenario harder to engineer than it appears. If it unfolds, Huckleberry Sting's strong recent form string (1-2312 on good) and consistent placed record make it the most dangerous closer, but it is racing out of its preferred role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Errors Decide
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors, falls or early departures significantly thin the field and reshape the tactical picture.
scenarios.body: In an 8-runner handicap chase on good ground, any incident at the fences — particularly involving the front-runners or prominent horses — throws the race wide open and brings Ribeye (an 11-year-old with experience over the trip) and Fast Deal back into contention through sheer survival. This scenario is the lowest-probability outcome but cannot be entirely dismissed in a competitive handicap chase where any of the field's error-prone histories could intervene.

watchPoints.text: La Quarite's 340-day absence is the single biggest risk in the race — if it blows up after pressing A Dublin Job through the first mile, the race shape collapses entirely and the tactical picture resets from halfway.

Cameron Johnstone-Baker claims 7lbs on A Dublin Job, reducing it to an effective 158lbs, but a claimer handling a front-runner in a contested lead duel over 2m5½f is a pressure point — watch for jumping errors or an inability to maintain rhythm under pressure.

Huckleberry Sting, Uncle Al, and Fast Deal are all natural hold-up horses unable to secure their preferred position in this shape — if all three are crowded into the middle of the field, the closing surge that might otherwise materialise may be blunted or come from the wrong part of the track.

Huit Reflets has been raised in trip from its recent 16-17f starts to 2m5½f here — watch whether Jamie Hamilton settles it conservatively in the early stages or pushes forward aggressively, as its stamina at this distance is unproven on good ground.

The Clonmel Kid's trainer Philip Kirby is 0/16 in the last 14 days — while yard form alone does not disqualify a horse, it is worth monitoring whether the runner comes into the race with the sharpness its profile demands.|

races.name: oddschecker.com Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: No More Bolero
runners_data.note: Won last two over 16f on good and has strong course profile (sim-going 11/15, 4W6P); wears hood, trained by James Owen who sends him in good form (LR 28d), and as confirmed sole front-runner gets a dream lead — STYLE_FIT tag reflects he is mapped as prominent but is clearly the race's de facto leader.

runners_data.name: God Of Fire
runners_data.note: Won over 18f good ground last time and ran well when second over 16f; Jonjo/AJ O'Neill yard quiet at 0/2 in 14 days but the horse's form profile (24/1) is progressive and he is a natural prominent type well placed to exploit any leader weakness.

runners_data.name: Four Decades
runners_data.note: Modest recent form string (8864-8) and a genuine hold-up horse who has yet to win in similar going (0W0P); Jack Andrews takes the ride for a yard with no runners in the 14-day window, and nothing in his profile suggests he can reverse recent modest efforts.

runners_data.name: Fine Point
runners_data.note: Won over 16f good on his penultimate start and placed twice more on similar ground (sim-going 12/15, 2W5P); wears a hood, a 5lb claimer takes over (Joshua Thompson), and his natural prominent style puts him right in the firing line in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Lone Star
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with solid placed record on good but consistently meets trips beyond his optimum (last five all 20f+); Philip Kirby yard quiet (0/16 in 14 days), and while he tracks the pace honestly, his advancing age and recent form (30-543) are against him.

runners_data.name: Ashdown Forest
runners_data.note: Won last time over 16f good, trained by Dan Skelton with Harry Skelton aboard — a formidable combination; a genuine hold-up type whose last win came on ground matching today's, though his OR of 96 means he faces tougher than that recent victory suggests.

runners_data.name: Ballynoe Boy
runners_data.note: Showed ability when third over 20f soft but the last two runs (8, 4 on good) are underwhelming; hold-up style needs a stronger pace than this race is likely to generate, and Nicky Richards' yard has had no runners in the 14-day window to signal sharpness.

runners_data.name: Quick Of The Night
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who is a genuine prominent racer by inclination but, with too many pace rivals present, has been mapped to midfield — a position that will blunt his effectiveness; recent form (65-330) is modest and the STYLE_FIT discount applies.

runners_data.name: Red Trail
runners_data.note: Modest OR of 74 and a form string featuring a pull-up (P) last time; a natural hold-up horse whose redistribution into midfield on the map reflects a crowded rear, and Charlie Maggs claims 3lb for a yard without a recent runner — hard to make a case here.

runners_data.name: Papillondelumiere
runners_data.note: Two recent pull-ups (PP) and rated just 73; a front-running type by nature who is mapped to midfield precisely because this race is already overloaded with prominent horses, meaning he is unlikely to get any position that suits — the redistribution compounds an already difficult profile.

races.paceDynamic: No More Bolero is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival likely to challenge for the lead from the outset, he should dictate a measured, sustainable gallop on good ground over 2m2½f. God Of Fire and Fine Point are natural prominent types who will sit directly behind him, creating a compact early order rather than a contested pace, which should keep the race from becoming a true stamina test. The field contains more prominent-minded horses than the race shape can accommodate — Quick Of The Night and Papillondelumiere are genuine prominent types who will be forced wider and further back than they prefer, while Red Trail is a true hold-up horse pushed into a mapped midfield position that flatters its tactical versatility. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting an honest but not frantic pace — strongly favours horses racing close to the pace from flag to finish, with prominent and tracking profiles best placed to pounce turning for home.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If No More Bolero dictates from the front and is never seriously pressured, setting a rhythm that suits horses racing in his slipstream.
scenarios.body: No More Bolero bowls along at a comfortable clip, the prominent brigade sits in behind on a tight rein, and the winner emerges from the front three or four turning in; pace-setters and close trackers are squarely in the box seat.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If No More Bolero fades in the closing stages and one of the natural prominent types comes through to assert.
scenarios.body: God Of Fire or Fine Point, sitting just off the leader throughout, finds the pace beginning to ease inside the final half-mile and picks up best of all; horses ridden with a prominent hold are the direct beneficiaries as the leader weakens.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field out and a genuine hold-up horse makes relentless late headway.
scenarios.body: Ashdown Forest or Ballynoe Boy, ridden patiently from further back, closes powerfully as the prominent horses empty near the final hurdle; this scenario requires a stronger gallop than appears likely given the single, unchallenged leader.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Causes Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If No More Bolero sets an unsustainably slow pace that compresses the field and produces a sprint finish from a big group.
scenarios.body: Horses with pace off a slow tempo — notably those with good turn-of-foot such as Ashdown Forest and Fine Point — benefit as the field bunches and a flat-out dash develops from the final hurdle; this scenario is unlikely given No More Bolero's recent front-running form and consistent recent wins.

watchPoints.text: No More Bolero's ability to control tempo unchallenged is the pivotal factor — watch whether God Of Fire or Fine Point push him from the outset, as any early pressure would transform the entire race shape.

Ashdown Forest carries the Skelton combination at the peak of their summer form; if he travels well in behind and the pace is strong enough to soften the front-runners, he could prove the biggest threat from off the pace.
Fine Point, wearing headgear and ridden by a 5lb claimer, has strong good-ground form — watch his position in the early stages, as prominent horses near the leader are best placed in this race shape.

Quick Of The Night and Papillondelumiere are both natural prominent types who may attempt to recover their preferred position early, potentially creating a brief scramble for places behind No More Bolero that could briefly lift the gallop.

Red Trail's last run ended in a pull-up — watch the pre-race market for any significant move that might suggest stable confidence has returned, as his current form and role make him difficult to assess on data alone.
